title: Protocol to isolate and culture primary mouse feto-placental endothelial cells
protocol: Euthanize the E15.5 pregnant female(s) by cervical dislocation in the morning.
Dissect the gravid uterus from the euthanized pregnant female.
Isolate individual E15.5 mouse conceptuses from the uterus.
Open the yolk sack of each conceptus carefully.
Separate the fetus, placenta, and yolk sack.
Identify the fetal side view of the E15.5 placenta to locate the darker, intensely vascularized central area corresponding to the labyrinthine zone (Lz).
Micro-dissect the labyrinthine zone (Lz) from the junctional zone (Jz) and decidua basalis (Db).
Collect Lz tissue from all E15.5 placentae in the litter.
Mince the collected Lz tissue into small fragments.
Place minced Lz tissue on ice under sterile conditions for further processing.
Avoid using inhaled CO2 or anesthetics for euthanasia of the pregnant mouse.
Open the abdomen and remove the uterus using scissors, placing it into a Petri dish containing ice-cold dissection media on ice.
Open the uterus and peel off all conceptuses using curved forceps.
Isolate each placenta by removing the yolk sac and sectioning the umbilical cord.
Transfer placentas to another Petri dish filled with ice-cold dissection media.
Isolate the Lz from each placenta under a dissecting microscope, removing the junctional zone and decidua basalis using Dumont tweezers #5 (straight) and #7 (curved).
Place all isolated placental Lz in a new Petri dish.
Wash placental Lz twice with ice-cold HBSS++ solution to remove excess blood.
Mince finely the Lz tissue using scalpels or small, sharp scissors.
Place the minced placental Lz tissue into a 50 mL Falcon tube filled with 20 mL pre-warmed collagenase-containing digestion solution.
Incubate for 1.5 hours at 37°C with gentle rotation (35 RPM).
Filter the digested tissue through a sterile 70-μm nylon mesh to remove clumps of cells or fragments of undigested tissue.
Press tissue through the filter with a cell lifter to ensure maximal cell recovery.
Pellet the cells by gentle centrifugation for 5 minutes at 260 × g in a centrifuge pre-chilled at 4°C.
Gently aspirate the supernatant (the pellet may be loose).
Wash the cells once with 20 mL ice-cold HBSS++ solution.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold HBSS++ solution, then mix with the remaining 19 mL.
Repeat step washing carefully without disturbing or aspirating the cell pellet.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 3 mL ice-cold Beads Buffer and transfer to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Mix 3 mL Beads Buffer for Lz tissue from one standard litter of 6-8 conceptuses.
Adjust volume of Beads Buffer when working with different amounts of placental tissue.
Resuspend sheep anti-rat IgG magnetic beads suspension by gentle shaking.
Transfer 8–10 μL of sheep anti-rat IgG Dynabeads into a sterile 2.0 mL round bottom microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of Beads Buffer and gently mix by pipetting.
Place the Eppendorf tube on the DynaMag magnetic stand and allow separation for approximately 1 minute.
Aspirate the solution without disturbing the beads.
Repeat the wash twice (total three washes).
Re-suspend washed beads in 1 mL of Beads Buffer by gentle pipetting.
Add 1.2 μL rat anti-mouse CD31 antibody to 10 μL Dynabeads and mix by gentle pipetting.
Allow antibody to bind to the beads for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rotation (35 RPM).
Wash the beads three times using the magnetic stand to remove unbound antibody.
Re-suspend the beads in the original volume of Beads Buffer (8–10 μL).
Add the re-suspended beads to the 15 mL Falcon tube containing the single-cell placental Lz suspension.
Incubate the Falcon tube for 1 hour at 4°C with slow rotation (35 RPM).
Transfer the beads + cells suspension into three 2 mL microfuge tubes placed on the DynaMag magnetic rack.
Collect beads and bound cells by placing the tubes on a magnet for 1 minute.
Remove and discard the bead-free cell suspension.
Wash the beads in each tube with 1 mL room temperature Beads Buffer.
Gently pipette to avoid foam or bubbles during washing.
Place the tubes back on the magnetic rack for 1 minute.
Carefully aspirate and discard the bead-free Beads Buffer.
Pool all beads into one single tube by resuspending beads from one tube in 1 mL Beads Buffer.
Transfer the resuspended bead solution to the second tube.
Gently mix the two aliquots of beads.
Transfer the mixed bead solution back to the last tube, pooling all beads in 1 mL of Beads Buffer.
Wash the beads three more times with 1 mL room temperature Beads Buffer each time.
Resuspend the bead-bound cells in 1 mL FPEC growth medium without heparin, pre-warmed at 37°C.
Transfer bead-bound cells to two wells of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Add 1.5 mL FPEC growth medium without heparin to each well for a total of 2 mL media/well.
Incubate the plate in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C under 5% CO2 and 5% O2.
Maintain primary endothelial cells in growth medium for at least four days after seeding.
Gently aspirate the medium and perform an additional wash, using 1 mL FPEC growth medium without heparin, to remove dead cells.
Feed the cells with 2 mL FPEC growth medium without heparin every other day until they reach 70%–80% confluence.
Remove media from wells when ready for first passage.
Add 0.2 mL Accutase pre-warmed at 37°C and incubate for 5 min at 37°C to detach cells.
Alternatively, use a trypsin-EDTA solution to detach FPEC; the incubation time depends on the trypsin concentration (2–3 min for a 0.25% trypsin solution; 5–6 min for a 0.05% trypsin solution).
Add 1.8 mL media into the well and transfer cells to a microcentrifuge tube.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 260 × g for 3 min.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant and re-suspend cell pellet evenly in 1 mL of FPEC growth medium with heparin.
Add 0.5 mL cell suspension into two wells of a new 6-well tissue culture plate.
Place the plate back in the incubator.
Place sterilized coverslips into the desired number of wells of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Add 400 μL of the gelatin-coating solution to each well.
Incubate the coverslips for 10 minutes at room temperature inside a laminar flow hood.
Remove the gelatin-coating solution by gentle aspiration.
Air-dry the coverslips for 15 minutes.
Seed approximately 5,000 cells in 500 μL of FPEC growth medium with heparin in each well containing gelatin-coated coverslips.
Incubate the plate in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C under 5% CO2 and 5% O2 for approximately 4–5 days, until the cells reach the desired density (80%).
Feed the cells on alternate days.
Remove the culture media from each well by gentle aspiration.
Wash twice with 500 μL PBS.
Add 500 μL of 2% formaldehyde solution to each well.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature.
Alternatively, add 500 μL of 4% formaldehyde solution directly into the culture medium.
Replace the pre-fixation culture medium with 500 μL of 2% formaldehyde solution after 2 min.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash the wells twice with 500 μL PBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Block non-specific staining by adding 400 μL of blocking buffer to each well.
Incubate for 45 min at room temperature.
Remove the blocking buffer without rinsing.
Dilute the unconjugated primary antibody (rabbit polyclonal anti-CD31) 1:50 in staining buffer, supplemented with 1% normal donkey serum.
Add 400 μL per well and incubate overnight at 2°C–8°C.
Include a negative control well using rabbit IgG antibody diluted 1:50 in staining buffer, supplemented with 1% normal donkey serum.
Wash twice with 400 μL of PBS supplemented with 0.05% Tween 20 for 5 min per wash at room temperature.
Dilute the secondary antibody (donkey anti-rabbit-AF594) 1:250 in staining buffer, supplemented with 1% normal donkey serum.
Add 400 μL of diluted secondary antibody to each well.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h in the dark.
Wash two times in 400 μL PBS-T (5 min each).
Add 300 μL of 5 μM DAPI solution in PBS to each well.
Incubate 2–5 min at room temperature.
Rinse once with PBS and once with water (5 min each).
Carefully remove the coverslips from the wells and blot to remove any excess water.
Dispense 1 drop of antifade mountant onto the microscope slide per coverslip.
Mount the coverslip with the cells facing towards the microscope slide.
Remove culture media from confluent FPEC wells in a 6-well plate.
Wash each well twice with 1 mL PBS at room temperature.
Add 0.2 mL pre-warmed Accutase per well and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Transfer the cells into a microcentrifuge tube after adding 1.8 mL media to each well.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation (400 × g for 5 min at 4°C) and discard supernatant.
Wash cells once with 1 mL of 0.1% BSA in PBS.
Pellet the cells as above after washing.
Re-suspend the cells in a small volume of PBS (e.g., 100 μL).
Use a small aliquot (10 μL) to count the cells.
Resuspend cells at 1 × 10^7 cells/mL in staining buffer.
Prepare one aliquot of 1 million cells (100 μL volume) for each experimental sample and place it in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add another 100 μL staining buffer to all tubes, reaching a final volume of 200 μL per tube.
Add 1 μg anti-CD16/32 antibody per 1 million cells to block Fc receptors and incubate on ice for 20 min.
At the end of blocking, add 0.25 μg of rat anti-mouse CD31-AF647 antibody in the CD31 control and experimental samples.
Incubate all tubes on ice in the dark for 1 h.
Add 800 μL staining buffer to all tubes after incubation and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and wash cells once more with 1 mL staining buffer.
Resuspend cells in 0.5 mL PBS and filter through 70-μm cell strainers into 5 mL polystyrene test tubes.
Add 5 μL 7-AAD solution per tube to all sample tubes, including the 7-AAD control tube, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Perform flow cytometry analysis.
